scope: DERIVED from model FLOPs and forced operand traffic. NOT HBM-measured. bw_lb_gbps = minimum effective traffic rate to achieve the observed device time; utilization_vs_peak compares MODEL effective TFLOP/s to the repo reference peak, it is NOT a matrix-unit counter activity.
hardware_status: unverified (PCM BLOCKED - no HBM bytes / matrix-unit activity)

headroom_by_shape.method: per-shape ideal time = FLOPs/(139.2e12) [ms]; headroom = device_ms - ideal_ms (clamped >=0); summed over the backward dW/dX rows of each tier
headroom_by_shape.window: SINGLE-STEP window: the per-shape rows come from ONE training step (kernel_efficiency_r36, step 2). Every device_ms / headroom_ms in this block is per step-2 window; 772.12 ms is the 3-step mean backward-GEMM time and is a different window.
headroom_by_shape.coverage_note: single-step rows (718.73 ms, step 2) and the 3-step mean (772.12 ms) are DIFFERENT windows; no coverage % and no 'uncovered' ms is derived from them (the previously derived coverage percentage and uncovered-ms figures are removed).
headroom_by_shape.window_note: the 100 per-shape rows come from ONE training step (kernel_efficiency_r36, step 2); 772.12 ms is the 3-step mean backward-GEMM time. 718.73/772.12 is reported as a RATIO BETWEEN DIFFERENT WINDOWS, not a same-window coverage percentage.
headroom_by_shape.retraction: The earlier 'up to ~285 ms/step' = (1-0.63)*772 from the 6-row 63% floor is RETRACTED. per-shape headroom = device_ms - FLOPs/peak is the ideal-device-time gap UNDER THE 139.2 REFERENCE ASSUMPTION; it is NOT an end-to-end ceiling.
headroom_by_shape.regroup_note: round-58 (review 7182886976 item 3): the two [1024,5120,1024] rows move from the short tier to the long tier (5120 flattened tokens); the two loss matmuls ([40,10,1024] dW and [10,40,1024] dX) are listed separately. Previous values: mid 113.91 / long 87.16 / short 47.65 ms.
headroom_by_shape.token_dim_rule: flattened-token dim = the operand dimension of [M,K,N] that is NOT a fixed model dimension (1024 / 4096): [4096,5120,1024] -> 5120 (K), [5120,1024,1024] -> 5120 (M), [1024,5120,1024] -> 5120 (K, was 1024 under the previous dX-takes-M rule). Rows with neither M nor K a model dimension are the loss matmuls (listed separately). Both model dims -> dW takes K, dX takes M. The old max(M,K) rule counted the fixed FFN feature dim 4096 as a long sequence (review BqpXfeg item 4).

bw_lb_caveat: bw_lb_gbps = forced_bytes_lb / (device_ms*1e6): LOGICAL byte rate assuming each operand is read/written ONCE per call. It is NOT an HBM measurement (cache reuse and repeated reads change real HBM traffic) and NOT a 'bandwidth lower bound' (renamed per review). Real HBM traffic needs PCM counters (BLOCKED).
unit_fix_note: FIXED round-51: previous bw_lb used bytes/(ms*1e-6)/1e9 = 1000x too large (S=512 dW showed 124,754 GB/s instead of 124.75). All bw values and conclusions derived from them corrected; 'strongly compute-bound' downgraded to a hypothesis to verify.
critical_path_method: per step: window=[first marker start, next step start); busy = UNION of clipped kernel+memcpy+memset intervals (NOT a sum of durations); idle=window-busy; overlap=|K|+|M|-|K u M|

conclusion.situation_1_compute_efficiency: 6 hot backward-GEMM shapes run at 88.1-129.25 TFLOP/s = 63%-93% of the 139.2 reference. Per-shape headroom (device_ms - FLOPs/139.2e12, the ideal-device-time gap under that reference, NOT an end-to-end ceiling) over 100 backward dW/dX rows of step 2 = 248.73 ms; by token-dim group: long (flattened tokens >= 4000): 99.91 ms over 353.48 ms device (20 rows); mid (1400 <= flattened tokens < 4000): 113.91 ms over 324.79 ms device (60 rows); short (flattened tokens < 1400): 34.67 ms over 40.23 ms device (18 rows). The 3-step mean backward GEMM (772.12 ms) is a different window and is not divided by these single-step rows. The earlier 'up to 285 ms/step' extrapolation is RETRACTED.
conclusion.situation_2_logical_traffic: dW arithmetic intensity 656-706 FLOP/byte; logical byte rate (each operand read/written once) 124-126 GB/s on the S=512 shapes. Whether the GEMMs are compute-bound is a HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY: it needs real HBM counters (BLOCKED) because cache reuse and repeated reads change the actual traffic. No 'strongly compute-bound' claim is made.
conclusion.situation_2_contiguous_copy: the .contiguous() copy FlagGems mm performs on a transposed A adds 8053.06 MB (S=512 dW-up) and 2013.27 MB (S=512 dW-down) of extra read+write per shape per step - a real extra traffic item, counted SEPARATELY from the GEMM body; it is why native+contiguous() loses (+32.4 ms median) while FlagGems still gains (its Triton kernel is faster on the contiguous operand by more than the copy costs)
conclusion.situation_3_idle_large: per-step idle 211-250 ms (87.9-91.5% busy) - idle is 8%-12% of the step and is NOT attributable without a host swimlane (needs counters/platform)
conclusion.ranking: backward GEMM (38%) > backward attention (18.5%) > forward GEMM (16.2%) > forward attention (10.1%)
conclusion.direction: (a) backward GEMM (38%) has the largest absolute headroom but its effective TFLOP/s (88-129) is already 63%-93% of reference -> vendor-side kernel tuning, not application-level; the transposed-view dW shapes (88 TF/s, 63%) are the weakest - a vendor fast path for transposed operands would target ~27 ms/step of the 258 ms dW time at most; (b) attention (fwd+bwd ~28.6%) runs at 12-13 TFLOP/s model-math over STAGE time - NOT comparable to the GEMM peak (softmax/dropout/masking are inside the stage time) -> needs a training-capable SDPA candidate (FlagGems ruled out); (c) idle 8-12% (211-250 ms/step) -> submission gaps or exposed copies, NOT attributable without a host swimlane
conclusion.platform_assistance: PCM window (pg-exporter), equivalent counter tool, vendor confirmation of metric level - see hbm_blocked_r46.md
